Hello. As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure and identified the issue. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

This error indicates that the primary dependency for Laghos, the MFEM library, has not been compiled before the Laghos application itself is built.

### Root Cause Analysis

The root cause of this issue lies in how the `make` command is being invoked. The `Laghos` Makefile contains a check that verifies the existence of the compiled MFEM library (`libmfem.a`) at the beginning of its execution.

When you run `RUN make parallel ...`, you are telling `make` to build only the `parallel` target. The Makefile's dependency-checking logic is structured in such a way that this specific target does not correctly trigger the prerequisite build of the MFEM library before performing the check. This causes the build to fail immediately.

The standard procedure for building this project from a clean state is to invoke `make` without a specific target, which defaults to the `all` target. The `all` target is correctly configured to build all dependencies (including MFEM) before compiling the Laghos executables. The `MFEM_USE_MPI=YES` flag correctly ensures that MFEM is built with MPI support, which is necessary for the parallel version of Laghos.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, you must change the `make` command to build the default `all` target instead of the specific `parallel` target. This will ensure the dependencies are built in the correct order. The subsequent `cp` command correctly copies the parallel executable (`laghos`), so no further changes are needed.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Use a standard Ubuntu LTS image as the base for our CPU build environment
FROM ubuntu:20.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to avoid prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers, MPI libraries, git, and certificates.
# build-essential: Provides make, gcc, etc.
# g++, gfortran: C++ and Fortran compilers required by Laghos and its dependencies.
# git: For cloning the source code repository.
# ca-certificates: For secure HTTPS connections during package downloads and git clones.
# openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: Provides the MPI runtime (mpirun) and development headers
# needed to compile MPI applications.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a temporary directory for cloning and building the source code
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the repository's default (latest) branch and its submodules recursively.
# The main Makefile also has a fallback to clone mfem if this step fails.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository
WORKDIR /build/Laghos

# Build the project. Invoking the default 'all' target ensures that dependencies
# like MFEM are built first before the main application. The MFEM_USE_MPI=YES
# flag ensures the parallel version of the dependency is built.
RUN make -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES

# Create a clean final directory for the application runtime files
RUN mkdir -p /app
WORKDIR /app

# As instructed, copy all problem data files from the source code's data
# directory into the final working directory.
RUN cp -r /build/Laghos/data/* .

# As instructed, copy the compiled executable to a standard system location
# that is on the default PATH. This makes the application directly runnable.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Clean up the build directory and source code to minimize the final image size
RUN rm -rf /build

# Set the entrypoint to the application executable.
# The user will typically provide the full command in their Kubernetes job spec,
# including the MPI launcher, e.g., `mpirun -np 4 laghos --problem 1`
ENTRYPOINT ["laghos"]
```

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

This error indicates that the primary dependency for Laghos, the MFEM library, has not been compiled before the Laghos application itself is built.

### Root Cause Analysis

The root cause of this issue lies in how the `make` command is being invoked. The `Laghos` Makefile contains a check that verifies the existence of the compiled MFEM library (`libmfem.a`) at the beginning of its execution.

When you run `RUN make parallel ...`, you are telling `make` to build only the `parallel` target. This causes the build to fail immediately.

The standard procedure for building this project from a clean state is to invoke `make` without a specific target, which defaults to the `all` target. The `all` target is correctly configured to build all dependencies (including MFEM) before compiling the Laghos executables. The `MFEM_USE_MPI=YES` flag correctly ensures that MFEM is built with MPI support, which is necessary for the parallel version of Laghos.

To resolve this, you must change the `make` command to build the default `all` target instead of the specific `parallel` target. This will ensure the dependencies are built in the correct order. Hello. As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure and identified the issue. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

This error indicates that the primary dependency for Laghos, the MFEM library, has not been compiled before the Laghos application itself is built.

### Root Cause Analysis

The root cause of this issue lies in how the `make` command is being invoked. The `Laghos` Makefile contains a check that verifies the existence of the compiled MFEM library (`libmfem.a`) at the beginning of its execution.

When you run `RUN make parallel ...`, you are telling `make` to build only the `parallel` target. The Makefile's dependency-checking logic is structured in such a way that this specific target does not correctly trigger the prerequisite build of the MFEM library before performing the check. This causes the build to fail immediately.

The standard procedure for building this project from a clean state is to invoke `make` without a specific target, which defaults to the `all` target. The `all` target is correctly configured to build all dependencies (including MFEM) before compiling the Laghos executables. The `MFEM_USE_MPI=YES` flag correctly ensures that MFEM is built with MPI support, which is necessary for the parallel version of Laghos.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, you must change the `make` command to build the default `all` target instead of the specific `parallel` target. This will ensure the dependencies are built in the correct order. The subsequent `cp` command correctly copies the parallel executable (`laghos`), so no further changes are needed.

    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \

    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

This error indicates that the primary dependency for Laghos, the MFEM library, has not been compiled before the Laghos application itself is built.

### Root Cause Analysis

The root cause of this issue lies in how the `make` command is being invoked. The `Laghos` Makefile contains a check that verifies the existence of the compiled MFEM library (`libmfem.a`) at the beginning of its execution.

When you run `RUN make parallel ...`, you are telling `make` to build only the `parallel` target. The Makefile's dependency-checking logic is structured in such a way that this specific target does not correctly trigger the prerequisite build of the MFEM library before performing the check. This causes the build to fail immediately.

The standard procedure for building this project from a clean state is to invoke `make` without a specific target, which defaults to the `all` target. The `all` target is correctly configured to build all dependencies (including MFEM) before compiling the Laghos executables. The `MFEM_USE_MPI=YES` flag correctly ensures that MFEM is built with MPI support, which is necessary for the parallel version of Laghos.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, you must change the `make` command to build the default `all` target instead of the specific `parallel` target. This will ensure the dependencies are built in the correct order. The subsequent `cp` command correctly copies the parallel executable (`laghos`), so no further changes are needed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

This error indicates that the primary dependency for Laghos, the MFEM library, has not been compiled before the Laghos application itself is built.

### Root Cause Analysis

The root cause of this issue lies in how the `make` command is being invoked. The `Laghos` Makefile contains a check that verifies the existence of the compiled MFEM library (`libmfem.a`) at the beginning of its execution.

When you run `RUN make parallel ...`, you are telling `make` to build only the `parallel` target. The Makefile's dependency-checking logic is structured in such a way that this specific target does not correctly trigger the prerequisite build of the MFEM library before performing the check. This causes the build to fail immediately.

The standard procedure for building this project from a clean state is to invoke `make` without a specific target, which defaults to the `all` target. The `all` target is correctly configured to build all dependencies (including MFEM) before compiling the Laghos executables. The `MFEM_USE_MPI=YES` flag correctly ensures that MFEM is built with MPI support, which is necessary for the parallel version of Laghos.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, you must change the `make` command to build the default `all` target instead of the specific `parallel` target. This will ensure the dependencies are built in the correct order. The subsequent `cp` command correctly copies the parallel executable (`laghos`), so no further changes are needed.

Hello. As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure and identified the issue. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

This error indicates that the primary dependency for Laghos, the MFEM library, has not been compiled before the Laghos application itself is built.

### Root Cause Analysis

The root cause of this issue lies in how the `make` command is being invoked. The `Laghos` Makefile contains a check that verifies the existence of the compiled MFEM library (`libmfem.a`) at the beginning of its execution.

When you run `RUN make parallel ...`, you are telling `make` to build only the `parallel` target. The Makefile's dependency-checking logic is structured in such a way that this specific target does not correctly trigger the prerequisite build of the MFEM library before performing the check. This causes the build to fail immediately.

The standard procedure for building this project from a clean state is to invoke `make` without a specific target, which defaults to the `all` target. The `all` target is correctly configured to build all dependencies (including MFEM) before compiling the Laghos executables. The `MFEM_USE_MPI=YES` flag correctly ensures that MFEM is built with MPI support, which is necessary for the parallel version of Laghos.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, you must change the `make` command to build the default `all` target instead of the specific `parallel` target. This will ensure the dependencies are built in the correct order. The subsequent `cp` command correctly copies the parallel executable (`laghos`), so no further changes are needed.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Use a standard Ubuntu LTS image as the base for our CPU build environment
FROM ubuntu:20.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers to avoid prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, compilers, MPI libraries, git, and certificates.
# build-essential: Provides make, gcc, etc.
# g++, gfortran: C++ and Fortran compilers required by Laghos and its dependencies.
# git: For cloning the source code repository.
# ca-certificates: For secure HTTPS connections during package downloads and git clones.
# openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: Provides the MPI runtime (mpirun) and development headers
# needed to compile MPI applications.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a temporary directory for cloning and building the source code
WORKDIR /build

# Clone the repository's default (latest) branch and its submodules recursively.
# The main Makefile also has a fallback to clone mfem if this step fails.
RUN git clone --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Set the working directory to the cloned repository
WORKDIR /build/Laghos

# Build the project. Invoking the default 'all' target ensures that dependencies
# like MFEM are built first before the main application. The MFEM_USE_MPI=YES
# flag ensures the parallel version of the dependency is built.
RUN make -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES

# Create a clean final directory for the application runtime files
RUN mkdir -p /app
WORKDIR /app

# As instructed, copy all problem data files from the source code's data
# directory into the final working directory.
RUN cp -r /build/Laghos/data/* .

# As instructed, copy the compiled executable to a standard system location
# that is on the default PATH. This makes the application directly runnable.
RUN cp /build/Laghos/laghos /usr/local/bin/

# Clean up the build directory and source code to minimize the final image size
RUN rm -rf /build

# Set the entrypoint to the application executable.
# The user will typically provide the full command in their Kubernetes job spec,
# including the MPI launcher, e.g., `mpirun -np 4 laghos --problem 1`
ENTRYPOINT ["laghos"]

Hello. As a debugging expert, I've analyzed the build failure and identified the issue. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

### Error Identification

The build is failing with the error message: `makefile:134: *** The MFEM library is not built. Stop.`

This error indicates that the primary dependency for Laghos, the MFEM library, has not been compiled before the Laghos application itself is built.

### Root Cause Analysis

The root cause of this issue lies in how the `make` command is being invoked. The `Laghos` Makefile contains a check that verifies the existence of the compiled MFEM library (`libmfem.a`) at the beginning of its execution.

When you run `RUN make parallel ...`, you are telling `make` to build only the `parallel` target. The Makefile's dependency-checking logic is structured in such a way that this specific target does not correctly trigger the prerequisite build of the MFEM library before performing the check. This causes the build to fail immediately.

The standard procedure for building this project from a clean state is to invoke `make` without a specific target, which defaults to the `all` target. The `all` target is correctly configured to build all dependencies (including MFEM) before compiling the Laghos executables. The `MFEM_USE_MPI=YES` flag correctly ensures that MFEM is built with MPI support, which is necessary for the parallel version of Laghos.
